title: Install Windows 11 from a USB drive
description: Check the requirements, make a bootable installer, boot from it and complete a clean installation.
objectives: Check that a computer meets the Windows 11 requirements.
Create a bootable Windows 11 USB drive with Microsoft's Media Creation Tool.
Boot from the USB drive using the boot menu.
Complete a clean installation and check activation and drivers.
tools: USB flash drive, 8 GB or larger (it will be erased)
A working PC with internet access
Genuine Windows licence or digital entitlement

safety.text: A clean installation erases the selected drive. Back up the customer's files first and confirm which drive you are installing to.
Only use Windows from Microsoft and genuine licences. Never use "activators" or modified installers: they are illegal and commonly contain malware.

steps.title: Check the requirements
steps.body:
Windows 11 needs at least:

- A compatible 64-bit processor, 1 GHz or faster with 2 or more cores
- **4 GB RAM** and **64 GB** storage
- **UEFI** firmware with **Secure Boot** capability
- **TPM 2.0**
- A DirectX 12 compatible graphics card

Microsoft's **PC Health Check** app tells you whether a computer qualifies. TPM and Secure Boot are often just switched off in the UEFI settings.

steps.title: Back up the data
steps.body: Copy the customer's documents, photos, browser data and any licence keys for their software to an external drive or cloud storage. Confirm the backup opens before you continue.

steps.title: Create the installation USB
steps.body:
1. On a working PC, download the **Media Creation Tool** from Microsoft's Windows 11 download page.
2. Insert a USB drive of 8 GB or more. **Everything on it will be erased.**
3. Run the tool, choose the language and edition, select **USB flash drive** and pick your drive.
4. Wait for it to download and finish.

steps.title: Boot from the USB drive
steps.body:
1. Insert the USB drive into the computer and turn it on.
2. Press the **boot menu key** right away. It differs by maker: commonly **F12, F11, F9, F8** or **Esc**.
3. Choose the USB drive, listed under UEFI.

If it does not appear, enter the UEFI setup (often **Del** or **F2**) and check the boot order and that USB boot is enabled.

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.body:
1. Choose your language, keyboard and click **Install now**.
2. Enter a product key, or choose **I don't have a product key** if the PC had Windows activated before: it activates automatically from its digital licence.
3. Choose the correct edition (the one the licence covers).
4. Choose **Custom: Install Windows only**.
5. Select the target drive. To start clean, delete its old partitions and install to the **unallocated space**: Windows creates the partitions it needs.

Double-check the drive size so you do not erase the wrong disk.

steps.title: Finish setup and check the system
steps.body:
1. Follow the setup screens (region, account, privacy).
2. Run **Windows Update** until no more updates are offered; it installs most drivers.
3. Open **Device Manager** and check for devices with a yellow warning icon. Install missing drivers from the computer or motherboard maker's website.
4. Check activation in **Settings → System → Activation**.
5. Restore the customer's files.

expectedResults: Windows 11 starts normally and is activated.
Device Manager shows no missing drivers.

commonMistakes.why: Deleting partitions on the wrong disk destroys data that may not be backed up.
commonMistakes.fix: Identify the drive by its size, and disconnect extra data drives during installation if unsure.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming an old PC cannot run Windows 11 because the check fails.
commonMistakes.why: TPM (often called fTPM or PTT) and Secure Boot are frequently just disabled in the UEFI settings.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the UEFI settings before deciding the hardware is unsupported.

commonMistakes.why: A Home licence will not activate Windows Pro, and the reverse.
commonMistakes.fix: Install the edition the licence covers.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which security features does Windows 11 require?
knowledgeChecks.answer: TPM 2.0 and UEFI with Secure Boot capability.

knowledgeChecks.question: How do you boot from the USB drive?
knowledgeChecks.answer: Press the boot menu key at startup (often F12, F11, F9, F8 or Esc, depending on the maker) and choose the USB drive.

knowledgeChecks.question: A PC had activated Windows before. Do you need a product key for a reinstall?
knowledgeChecks.answer: Usually not: choose "I don't have a product key" and it activates from its digital licence.

references: Microsoft: Windows 11 specifications and system requirements.
